correctness.rationale: The ridit variance and cut covariances are exact cell-midpoint identities. Every increasing score is a positive combination of centered cut indicators. The minimum cut correlation plus the triangle inequality gives the lower bound; strictness follows because at least two non-collinear cut indicators have positive coefficients when there are at least three categories. A one-dominant-gap family proves sharpness, while Cauchy--Schwarz and connectedness give the upper endpoint and interval filling.

value.rationale: Ordinal-score choice is a longstanding practical problem and published work explicitly warns that midrank/ridit choices can change conclusions. The theorem gives an exact profile-specific robustness envelope for the canonical ridit score, including the worst order-preserving recoding and a simple equal-frequency benchmark. It is a complete natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
